357.h: The Nigerian Maritime University is a federal university and the first maritime university in Nigeria. It was set up to address a chronic shortage of trained professionals and technical expertise in the maritime industry. In February 2018 the National Universities Commission approved it to start degree programmes, so that teaching could begin in the 2017/2018 session.
357.a: The university trains students for shipping, marine engineering, maritime transport and related industries.
357.c: Its permanent site is at Okerenkoko in Delta State, on the left bank of the Escravos River. The river is a busy route for shipping and inland water transport, and opens into the Atlantic Ocean, where vessels serving the oil and gas industry operate.

383.h: The Federal University of Environment and Technology (FUET) is one of Nigeria's newest federal universities; the National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2025. It is located in Ogoniland, in the south-east of Rivers State. Ogoniland's environment was badly damaged by oil production after crude oil was discovered there in commercial quantities in 1958, and the university's focus reflects that history.
383.a: The university offers undergraduate and graduate programmes in environmental studies and technology.
383.c: The university is at Koroma/Sakpenwa, in the Tai area of Ogoniland, Rivers State.

396.h: Wesley University, Ondo is a private Christian university founded by the Methodist Church Nigeria and licensed in 2007. It is named after John Wesley, the founder of Methodism. It continues a long Methodist record in Nigerian education: the church founded many primary and secondary schools, teacher-training colleges such as Wesley College, Ibadan, in 1905, and theological institutions.
396.a: The university aims to provide a broad education that trains students to reason well and to find or create employment. It offers undergraduate programmes and is licensed by the National Universities Commission.
396.c: It is located in Ondo town, Ondo State.

408.h: Spiritan University, Nneochi (SUN) is a private Catholic university established in 2017 by the Nigeria South-East Province of the Congregation of the Holy Spirit (the Spiritans), an international Catholic religious order founded in France on 27 May 1703. The Federal Executive Council approved and licensed it on 6 December 2017, on the recommendation of the National Universities Commission.
408.a: The university offers conventional undergraduate programmes, and its graduates are linked through an alumni network, Spiritan Alumni Connect.
408.c: It is located in Umunneochi, a rural local government area of Abia State.

411.h: Trinity University is a private university that grew out of a group of schools. Its founders opened Trinity International College in 1995, first at GRA Ikeja in Lagos, before moving it in 1998 to its own 83-acre site at Ofada, Ogun State. They added Trinity Foundation School, a primary school, at Ofada in 1996. The National Universities Commission records the university's establishment in 2019.
411.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and has announced new programmes in biochemistry, logistics management and cybersecurity.
411.c: It is located at Ofada, Ogun State, on the outskirts of Lagos.

414.h: Thomas Adewumi University (TAU) is a private university. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2021. Within two years it was hosting events such as the IndabaX machine-learning conference in 2023.
414.a: TAU offers more than 25 academic programmes.
414.c: The university is fully residential, with all students living on campus at Oko-Irese, Kwara State.

416.h: Ave Maria University, Piyanko (AMU) is a private Catholic university founded by the Ave Maria Foundation, which also runs the Ave Maria group of schools, including a nursery and primary school in Nyanya, Abuja. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2021.
416.a: The university offers courses leading to recognised undergraduate degrees.
416.c: It is located in Piyanko, Nasarawa State, within reach of Abuja.

433.h: Baba-Ahmed University, Kano (BAUK) is a private university licensed by the National Universities Commission in 2022. It admitted its pioneer students to faculties of Computing, Management and Social Sciences, and later launched a Faculty of Law, together with digital student portals and specialised technology laboratories.
433.a: Admission is through JAMB's UTME. The university publishes its own academic and examination regulations, with a second edition covering 2026 to 2030.
